Commentary.Commentary: Right then! The target for Pakistan is 279. Now the onus is on their batters and especially their openers who have been under a lot of criticism for slow starts. With Fakhar Zaman, it could change today. For Zimbabwe to win this, they need their bowlers to fire and fire early. Can the team from Africa win it or will Pakistan complete a whitewash? Do join us on the other side of the break for the chase.

Pakistan's bowling unlike Zimbabwe's batting blew hot and cold. They started on fire with Hasnain and Afridi in full flow. The former though was oozing fire as he sent the three Zimbabwean batsmen back to the pavillion inside the first Powerplay. Since then, it was a dry run for all the bowlers as the pair of Williams and Taylor grinded it out in the middle. Though Hasnain came back to snare a couple of wickets to complete his ODI 5-fer, the rest could not live up to the challenge. Afridi was once again wicketless, Muhammad Musa who made his debut in the last game was carted for 80 runs in his 10 overs. Wahab Riaz was wayward throughout this innings and Iftikhar Ahmed too did not have a great game. To add to it, a few dropped chances caused a bit more agony for Pakistan in the field. Poor from them after two brilliant bowling performances in the previous two ODIs.

A tale of two halves is what the Zimbabwean innings can be termed as. After opting to bat they once again got off to the worst start. Once again they lost their skipper Chamu Chibhabha for a nought to the returning Mohammad Hasnain. Craig Ervine and Brian Chari too could not offer any resistance against the Pakistan bowlers thunderbolts. Once again the onus fell on the experienced pair of Taylor and Williams who did not disappoint as they stitched an 84-run stand. Taylor reached his fifty in the process and just when things were looking a lot settled for the Rhodesians, Taylor departed. Zimbabwe though did not panic as Williams and the young Madhevere kept the Zimbabwean innings sailing as they stitched a 75-run stand. With Williams and Raza out there, Zimbabwe breached the 270-run mark and ended with a score of 278 runs. Williams too reached his 4th ODI ton and remained not out. A brilliant recovery from Zimbabwe after a long long time.

Zimbabwe are underway with a leg bye. Good length ball on the pads, Ervine looks to flick but it takes the pads and goes towards the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Full ball on the pads, Ervine looks to flick but gets hit on the pads.
Zimbabwean skipper, Chamu Chibhabha fails once again. Who will comes out to bat now? The experienced Craig Ervine walks out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! What a start from Hasnain and Pakistan. He strikes in his first over on his comeback. Brilliant delivery and Zimbabwe have lost an early wicket yet again. Back of a length ball on off, Chibhabha looks to defend but it takes the outside edge and goes towards Iftikhar Ahmed at second slip. He dives to his right and takes a good catch. Terrific start from Pakistan.
Back of a length ball outside off, Chibhabha lets the ball go to the keeper.
PLAY AND A MISS! Hasnain starts with a good length ball outside off, Chibhabha looks to cut but fails to get any bat on it.
Who will it be from the other end? Mohammad Hasnain it will be.
A maiden to start from Shaheen Afridi. Brilliant first over from him. Full ball angling in on off, Chari drives it towards mid off for a dot.
Good length ball on the pads, Chari looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Full ball outside off, Chari drives but finds the fielder at point.
Missing the stumps this time. Full ball on the pads, Chari looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. Afridi appeals but the umpire is not interested.
Full ball on middle, Chari looks to drive but gets it off the inside half of the bat towards mid-wicket.

Afridi starts with a lovely inswinger. He bowls it on middle, Chari looks to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads. Afridi appeals but nothing from the umpire. Good decision as there was a big inside edge on that.
We are all set to begin! The Pakistan players make their way out to the middle, followed by Chamu Chibhabha and Brian Chari. Shaheen Afridi will start with the ball.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Imam-ul-Haq, Fakhar Zaman (IN PLACE OF ABID ALI), Babar Azam (C), Haider Ali, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Iftikhar Ahmed, Khushdil Shah (IN PLACE OF FAHEEM ASHRAF), Mohammad Hasnain (IN PLACE OF IMAD WASIM), Wahab Riaz (IN PLACE OF HARIS RAUF), Shaheen Afridi, Muhammad Musa.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Chari, Chamu Chibhabha (C), Craig Ervine, Brendan Taylor (WK), Sean Williams, Wesley Madhevere, Sikandar Raza, Tendai Chisoro, Donald Tiripano (IN PLACE OF CARL MUMBA), Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Zimbabwe. They have elected to bat first.

A dead rubber? Think again! Even though the series is lost for Zimbabwe, they have plenty to play for as ICC World Cup Super League points are up for grab and they would be desperate to get their first points on the board. Pakistan, on the other hand, have been brilliant in the 2 ODIs so far and they look the favourites to make it 3-0. Faheem Ashraf has been ruled out of this game due to food poisoning so there will certainly be one change for Pakistan. Will they make any more changes to their line-up? We will find out soon as the toss is not far away. Hello and welcome to the final ODI between Pakistan and Zimbabwe.
